title.narrative: Activity under preparation Access to Water in Northern Ghana - EU-Ghana Partnership for smart and sustainable cities Phase 3

description.narrative: Following the ongoing phase 1 on urban planning and waste management (AAP 2022) and an imminent phase 2 on sanitation and flood prevention infrastructures (AAP 2024), the phase 3 of the sustainable cities initiative will focus on clean water access in four cities (Tamale, Damongo, Wa and Bolgatanga), which are among the six Northern cities covered by the EU-Ghana Partnership for sustainable cities. It is line with SDG 11.It includes the construction of a 135,000 m³/day Water Treatment Plant to meet the projected demand by 2040 on the Tamale ¿ Damongo axis and the expansion of distribution water pipe network in Tamale, Damongo and Wa (the latter already benefits from a an underused water treatment plant). To promote equitable access, public water points and households¿ connections will be rolled out in underserved areas in the four cities. A human rights-based approach will guide the initiative, ensuring marginalized populations will benefit through subsidized connections and flexible payment schemes. The decision-making process will consider density and affordability at specific locations, while trained local entities (private or associative) will manage public points. The system¿s management will be enhanced with a digital platform (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition - SCADA) to monitor operations across the new plant and remote sites. Finally, capacity building to Ghana Water Limited, the Ghanaian public utility in charge of urban water management will play a key role contributing on long term to assets¿ sustainability, quality of services, transparency and inclusivity.The sanitation and drainage infrastructure investments in phase 2 lay a technically sound and complementary groundwork for phase 3. Overall, the project will enable approximately one million Ghanaians to benefit from improved access to safe drinking water (SDG 5). It will also stimulate economic development, as reliable water supply is a critical enabler of growth.This action will be implemented through blending with the EIB and regional funds, while Invest International and DANIDA (Danish Development Cooperation under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs) will provide parallel financing. This comes in addition to the other partners¿ support to the urban development of six cities in the North of Ghana under the previous phases and with complementary actions, namely by Expertise France, AFD, UNICEF and Hungary.The action is aligned with the external dimension of the Global Gateway, EU Green Deal Strategy, the EU Gender Action Plan III (2020-2025), the EU Strategy on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, the EU¿s Action Plan on Human Rights and Democracy 2020-2024 and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
